entry.title: Postal codes of Spain
entry.content:
Estimated postal code areas from open data

2 min.

Códigos postales de España provides estimated postal code areas for Spain, built from open address data from CartoCiudad and administrative boundaries. Explore the results on interactive maps and download the data for use in R, Python or QGIS.

Background

Postal code polygons are useful for linking addresses and statistics to areas on a map. According to Goerlich (2022), the Correos polygons available through CartoCiudad stopped being offered for download in early 2017. This project explores a reproducible alternative based on open address data.

An early reference is José Ignacio Sánchez’s 2020 article in NoSoloSIG, which describes how to estimate postal areas from CartoCiudad addresses using GIS tools. This project applies the approach developed in Francisco José Goerlich’s 2022 work, with its own choices for selecting addresses and handling areas without an assignment.

Maps and data

The project website includes interactive maps and two GeoPackage downloads: a full version for spatial analysis and a simplified version for visualization. Both include postal code areas and administrative areas pending assignment.

The data is shared under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license.

Interactive map

Search for a postal code or address, select a two-digit prefix and compare the estimated areas with CartoCiudad. The viewer uses the simplified data and does not display areas pending assignment. Its controls are in Spanish.

Open the map in a full window Viewer guide

Methodology

Following Goerlich’s approach, the workflow treats each separate component of an administrative area independently. When the selected addresses share a single postal code, it assigns that code to the whole component. When several codes are present, it builds Voronoi polygons around the address locations, clips them to the administrative boundary and merges areas with the same code. The final polygons are dissolved by postal code across provinces.

This implementation selects addresses using an inward buffer of 200 m, with a second attempt at 50 m if none are found, rather than the 20 m described by Goerlich. Components without selected addresses remain unassigned unless the municipality has a single postal code recovered from its other components. The administrative boundaries come from LAU2boundaries4Spain, by Francisco José Goerlich and Pedro Pérez Vázquez.

These are estimated areas, not official postal boundaries. Coverage depends on the source addresses and some areas remain unassigned. The repository documents the sources, methodology, limitations and steps to reproduce the data.

References

  • Centro Nacional de Información Geográfica. (n.d.). CartoCiudad [Data set]. https://www.cartociudad.es/web/portal/
  • Correos. (n.d.). Base de datos de códigos postales y capa cartográfica [Product information]. Product page
  • Goerlich, F. J. (2022). Elaboración de un mapa de códigos postales de España con recursos libres: Cómo evitar pagar por disponer de información de referencia (Working Paper No. 2022-3). Ivie. https://doi.org/10.12842/WPIVIE_0322 (Updated online version)
  • Goerlich, F. J., & Pérez Vázquez, P. (2025). Base de datos histórica de contornos municipales de España –LAU2boundaries4Spain– (Version 2) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15345101
  • Hernangómez, D. (2026). Códigos postales de España (Version 1.0.0) [Data set]. Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23698418 (Project documentation)
  • Instituto Geográfico Nacional. (n.d.). Servicios de visualización de CartoCiudad: Direcciones y códigos postales [WMS documentation]. Service documentation
  • Sánchez, J. I. (2020, November 13). Así hice el mapa de los códigos postales de España con SIG y datos abiertos. Nosolosig. Article
entry.summary: Explore estimated postal code areas for Spain and download GeoPackage files for R, Python and QGIS.

entry.title: Large forest fires in Spain
entry.content:
EGIF reports, reconciled fire records and cartography with R

3 min.

GIFs brings together structured data on large forest fires in Spain and R code for an infographic inspired by Dominic Royé’s firefly cartography. Here, GIF means gran incendio forestal: a fire with at least 500 hectares of forest area burned.

The project combines exports from MITECO’s General Forest Fire Statistics (EGIF) with its annual reports and provisional updates. It preserves source information and reconciliation notes so that users can trace how records were selected, grouped and located.

Two related data products

The collection currently provides two complementary views:

  • EGIF reports: 329 selected reports from 2010–2023. Each row has a unique egif_part_id and includes source fields, burned areas, cause, provenance, notes and coordinates where they can be interpreted.
  • Reconciled fires: 455 fire records from 2010–2026, used by the infographic. Each fire has a stable fire_id; a fire may bring together several EGIF reports.

These are different units of observation. Do not add the two tables’ row counts or burned areas together. The 500-hectare threshold is applied after explicitly documented groupings of reports belonging to the same fire.

EGIF takes priority when a documented match exists. Records without a match retain their original MITECO annual report or provisional update. Reports awaiting reconciliation keep an empty fire_id and are not automatically added as new fires, which helps avoid double counting.

Coverage and limitations

The fire-level records span February 27, 2010 to September 26, 2026. These are the first and last dates in the file, not evidence of complete annual coverage. The project is not a real-time monitoring service.

The documented reconciliation still has nine earlier fire records and eight selected EGIF reports awaiting a match. Two additional records retain their provisional source because their province has no reports in the 2023 EGIF export. That export contains no records for seven provinces, so an absence from these files should not be interpreted as an absence of fires.

The methodology explains source priority, explicit groupings and unresolved cases. The data guide documents the source exports and processing. The original ZIP files are preserved with SHA-256 checksums.

Coordinates and the infographic

Geographic coordinates use EPSG:4326, keeping the Canary Islands in their actual location. EGIF coordinates are transformed only when their coordinate system can be interpreted. Missing coordinates or an unknown datum leave the geographic coordinates empty rather than producing an invented point.

The fire-level view uses interpretable EGIF coordinates where available and an identified municipal reference location otherwise. location_method distinguishes these sources. For fires with several reports, the view records which report supplies its reference point. Declared municipality codes and municipalities obtained through a spatial join are retained separately.

The points are reference locations, not fire perimeters. Municipal reference locations come from IGN through SIANE and mapSpain. The infographic reads the reconciled fire view and uses circle sizes to show forest area burned.

Downloads, citation and reuse

Both products are available in CSV, JSON and GeoJSON from the project website. Read identifiers and municipality codes as text to preserve their representation. JSON supplies explicit types and null values; GeoJSON retains records without usable coordinates with geometry: null.

Machine-readable field descriptions are provided separately in the EGIF report Croissant metadata and the fire-level Croissant metadata.

For reproducible analyses, cite the DOI of the version used. The collection’s version 2.0.0 DOI identifies the archived release; the general DOI groups the project’s releases.

Data reuse follows the MITECO legal notice, including attribution and preservation of the original conditions and metadata. The municipal cartography credits CartoBase ANE 2006–2024, CC BY 4.0, IGN. The repository’s MIT license applies to code and documentation. The project is independent and does not imply MITECO participation or endorsement.

References

  • Royé, D. (2021, June 1). Firefly cartography. Dr Dominic Royé. https://dominicroye.github.io/blog/firefly-maps/
entry.summary: Explore EGIF reports and reconciled records of large forest fires in Spain, with CSV, JSON and GeoJSON downloads and documented methodology.

entry.title: Celestial data
entry.content:
A compilation of celestial data files

1 min.

This project provides several datasets of celestial objects as of the J2000 epoch in GeoJSON and GeoPackage formats.

The original files were provided by the d3-celestial plugin (Frohn 2015) under BSD 3-Clause. The datasets produced by this project consist of the same data provided by the d3-celestial plugin processed with the R package sf (Pebesma 2018) to ensure its validity:

  • The spatial data objects are bounded by \([-180, -90, 180, 90]\).

  • The coordinates represent J2000 celestial directions in degrees. EPSG:4326 is assigned for compatibility with GIS software. The angles are right ascension and declination.

  • All geometries are valid as per ST_IsValid (GEOS 3.9.3).

Distribution

These URLs serve the same minified GeoJSON file from the main branch.

<!-- From GitHub -->
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dieghernan/celestial_data/main/data/mw.min.geojson

https://dieghernan.github.io/celestial_data/data/mw.min.geojson

<!-- From jsDelivr -->
https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/dieghernan/celestial_data@main/data/mw.min.geojson

Data

Data are provided in GeoJSON (*.geojson) and GeoPackage (*.gpkg) formats. Additionally, for GeoJSON files a minified version (*.min.geojson) is also provided.

entry.title: Corona Atlas
entry.content:
Historical international COVID-19 risk areas designated by German authorities

1 min.

Project discontinued. This page documents a historical project; the descriptions below refer to its period of operation.

Visit https://dieghernan.github.io/corona-atlas.de/

Interactive map of the international COVID-19 risk areas as designated by the German authorities.

During the project, data was updated periodically from the website of the Robert Koch Institute.

Data scraping is performed in Python with scrapy. The scraper also uses pandas and pycountry.

For the prototype version, map visualization was created with R and generated via rmarkdown using leaflet, giscoR and some packages included in the tidyverse. For the deployment, map logic has moved to JavaScript to support multiple languages.

Read more in this post
entry.summary: Historical interactive map of international COVID-19 risk areas, based on assessments by the German authorities during the project’s operation.

entry.title: spain-munic-bot
entry.content:
An archive of maps generated with R

1 min.

Project discontinued. This page documents a historical project; the descriptions below refer to its period of operation.

🤖 Twitter bot: random municipalities of Spain 🇪🇸 with mapSpain, posted with rtweet via a GitHub Action

I was a bot 🤖 that tweeted a random map of a Spanish municipality with its name, province and autonomous community (and an inset map of Spain showing the region and the community). I ran 🏃‍♀️ every 20 minutes.

I have a website!

Tweets by spainmunic

📦 R packages

Core packages used in the project are:

  • mapSpain for the location of the municipalities, base polygons, coordinates and imagery.
  • osmdata for the streets.
  • tmap for plotting.
  • rtweet for posting.

Other packages used are sf, dplyr and other common supporting packages.
entry.summary: Archived maps of buildings and urban growth in Spanish municipalities, generated with R. Automated posting is disabled.

entry.title: Leaflet-providersESP
entry.content:
Plugin for Leaflet.js

1 min.

Leaflet-providersESP is a plugin for Leaflet that contains configurations for various tile layers provided by public agencies in Spain.

Demo

Full docs and examples are available at https://dieghernan.github.io/leaflet-providersESP/.

This code generates a Leaflet map with a layer provided by Leaflet-providersESP.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <meta charset="utf-8" />
    <title>Minimal page | leaflet-providersESP</title>
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
    <!-- Load Leaflet -->
    <link
      rel="stylesheet"
      href="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.7.1/dist/leaflet.css"
    />
    <script src="https://unpkg.com/leaflet@1.7.1/dist/leaflet.js"></script>
    <!-- Install leaflet-providersESP -->
    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/dieghernan/leaflet-providersESP/dist/leaflet-providersESP.min.js"></script>
    <!-- Display map full page -->
    <style>
      html {
        height: 100%;
      }
      body {
        height: 100%;
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
      }
      #mapid {
        height: 100%;
        width: 100%;
      }
    </style>
  </head>
  <body>
    <!-- Create map -->
    <div id="mapid"></div>
    <!-- Puerta del Sol - IDErioja server -->
    <script>
      var mymap = L.map("mapid").setView([40.4166, -3.70384], 18);
      L.tileLayer.providerESP("IDErioja").addTo(mymap);
    </script>
  </body>
</html>

All providers

Open the map in a full window Documentation
entry.summary: Leaflet plugin for adding WMS/WMTS provided by public agencies in Spain.

entry.title: Country codes & organizations
entry.content:
A database with geocodes

2 min.

Complete database of countries and territories, their different country codes under common standards (ISO-3166, GEC (formerly FIPS), M49 (UN), STANAG (NATO), NUTS (EU), etc.) and their membership in different international organizations.

Note that blanks are presented as "" instead of NA since ISO-3166-ALPHA 2 for Namibia is NA.

Vignette: Using country codes

A. Country codes .csv

Main .csv file (link) containing:

  • Country and regional codes
  • Currency, dependency status and sovereignty information
  • Names in English and Spanish as provided by Unicode CLDR
  • Additional information (demographics, capital, area, etc.)

Codes included

Field Description Source Notes
ISO_3166_1 ISO 3166-1 numeric Wikipedia  
ISO_3166_2 ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 Wikipedia  
ISO_3166_3 ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 Wikipedia  
FIPS_GEC Geopolitical Entities and Codes (GEC) CIA World Factbook Formerly FIPS 1PUB 10-4 (historical CIA reference)
STANAG STANAG 1059 Country Codes CIA World Factbook Used by NATO
M49 UN Country Code UN Stats  
NUTS NUTS 0 code Wikipedia Used by EU
geonameId geonameId geonames  
continentcode geonames Continent Code geonames  
regioncode UN Regional Code UN Stats  
interregioncode Interregional Code UN Stats  
subregioncode Subregion Code UN Stats  
ISO_3166_3.sov Sovereign code Wikipedia, Statoids If non-independent

Other information included

  • Currency
  • Dependency status
  • Names in English and Spanish for countries, continents, regions and capitals
  • Population, area (km2) and developed region

B. International organizations .csv

A single .csv file (link) describing the membership status of each country across 186 international organizations.

    "member",
    ...
    ]
  },

]

A complementary function (intended to be used in R) has been developed:

ISO_memcol = function(df, #Input dataframe
                      orgtosearch #org id
) {
  ind = match(orgtosearch, unlist(df[1, "org_id"]))
  or = lapply(1:nrow(df), function(x)
    unlist(df[x, "org_member"])[ind])
  or = data.frame(matrix(unlist(or)), stringsAsFactors = F)
  names(or) = orgtosearch
  df2 = as.data.frame(cbind(df, or, stringsAsFactors = F))
  return(df2)
}

D. Data sources

  • Unicode Consortium. (n.d.). Unicode Common Locale Data Repository [Archived data]. GitHub. https://github.com/unicode-cldr
  • United Nations Statistics Division. (n.d.). Standard country or area codes for statistical use (M49). https://unstats.un.org/unsd/methodology/m49/overview/

entry.title: Bzel
entry.content:
A Pebble project

1 min.

Project discontinued due to the shutdown of Pebble.

Bzel integrates the bezel into your watch face. Display minutes as digits, as a moving dot or as a fill in the bezel.

Bzel uses the bezel as an extra space for displaying the minutes.

Download from Rebble Appstore

Features

  • Clock mode:
    • Digital: Minute display based on analog movement
    • Dot: Moving dot as a minute marker
    • Bezel: A bar moving around the bezel as a minute marker
  • Autodetection of 12h/24h mode based on your watch settings

Take your pick

  • Pebble Health: Display daily steps.
  • Date - Get the weekday based on the language set on your Pebble.
  • Weather: Current conditions in °C or °F.
  • Choose your weather provider:
    • Yahoo.com No API key required at this moment
    • Wunderground
    • OpenWeatherMap
  • Historical integration with Master Key (pmkey.xyz)
  • Location based on your selected weather provider
  • Night theme displayed between sunset and sunrise

Internationalization

Automatic weekday translation is supported for:

  • English
  • Spanish
  • German
  • French
  • Portuguese
  • Italian

Future developments

  • Location for weather
  • Square support
  • New minute mode: bezel
  • Steps
  • More health metrics

Screenshots

Minute progress displayed around the Pebble Time Round bezel.

The bezel minute indicator adapted to the Pebble Time screen.

Monochrome version of the bezel-based minute display.

Attributions

Fonts

  • Weather Icons by Eric Flowers, modified and fitted to the regular alphabet instead of Unicode values.
  • Custom font for icons created via Fontastic.
  • Gotham Fonts downloaded from fontsgeek.com

Weather providers

Others

Master Key (pmkey.xyz) was a service for Pebble users that managed API keys through a unique PIN.

License

Licensed under the MIT license.

Made in Madrid, Spain ❤️
entry.summary: Bzel integrates the bezel into your watch face. Display minutes as digits, as a moving dot or as a fill in the bezel.

    • Yahoo No API key required at this moment
    • Wunderground
    • OpenWeatherMap
  • Historical integration with Master Key (pmkey.xyz)

The watch face supports multiple languages and optional date formats.
